hypotheses.name: Optimization target remains unidentified; small model gains may optimize the wrong ranking
evidence: Same v1 predictions score .575601 on all80, .394064 on top5count80, .237792 on top5seconds80, .439352 on top5count30 in main local window. This label-choice effect greatly exceeds recent feature/model deltas.
Official wording says five most preferred programmes; output length does not prove hidden truth length or preference formula.80percent rule came from participant description.
Three public outcomes cannot identify one target among several correlated proxies; score closeness is not evidence of exact semantics.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Inspect organizer target-generation/evaluation code or exact stated formula: overlap denominator, strict/inclusive threshold, airing/session aggregation, all-items versus preferred subset, count versus duration preference, ties, empty users. Reproduce on a small historical example; request no hidden test labels.
hypotheses.budget: Documentation/code inspection only initially; <=5min CPU and1GB for historical reconstruction if exact logic supplied; zero fitting/submission.
hypotheses.strategy_change: If exact rule differs, rebuild labels and reassess frozen predictions before training. If unavailable, retain all80 and top5count80 as declared plausible targets with explicit uncertainty; do not choose a proxy because it matches Kaggle.
hypotheses.risk: Overinterpreting a participant description or adapting proxy definitions to three leaderboard observations.

hypotheses.name: Horizon, user participation and session structure create larger transport shift than model capacity
evidence: Fitting history35days, outer70days, later105days, final140days; label horizons range14/21/35/70days while deployment forecast84days.
Raw population sessions/day61904 in early fitting history versus26812 in main validation.

No-retrieved-positive fitting groups455/4721 early versus1724/4813 recent; filtering recent+early improves .462831 to .486095 but remains below filtered early .491881 under all80 HGB. This does not falsify target-matched ranking, but exposes cohort selection.

Sample22925 raw sessions had0exact duplicates yet10321different-channel overlap pairs and556same-channel overlapping pairs. These may be concurrent household/device use; do not assume a single uninterrupted personal viewing process.
Raw session duration maximum342145seconds. The current weekly context caps each session to3600 weighted seconds, while label construction can credit many complete airings from one long session.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Before fitting, quantify top5 stability and activity eligibility across nested14/35/70day windows, plus preferred-airing contributions from long sessions and concurrent-channel sessions. Compare source/category AP by target-user activity/cohort using only pre-cut features for strata. Then one paired horizon/population experiment on fixed evaluation rows, not a grid.
hypotheses.budget: <=3min CPU/1GB for cached/raw diagnostic aggregation; any new1-2fits require explicit approval and a separate small budget.
hypotheses.strategy_change: If target ranks vary strongly with horizon, prioritize programme opportunity/completion-count prediction and horizon-aware aggregation. If selected-user participation dominates, design target-cohort training or weighting from pre-cut variables. If long channel sessions dominate relevant labels, test channel-run completion features rather than treating concurrent logs as corrupt.
hypotheses.risk: 20weeks of logs cannot supply long historical fit plus12week supervised labels plus an independent12week holdout. A May4-Jul27 outer test would leak current v3 labels throughMay18; refit must end labels byMay4. Newer/longer targets also change season/cohort, so effects must not be attributed to horizon alone.

hypotheses.name: Potential gains split between seen-item ordering and user-new globally-known programmes; generic expansion lacks the needed conditional ranking signal
evidence: Main top5 source idealmass: seen .67294 versus actualAPcredit .40018; new-user/global-known .26526 versus actual .00724; globallynew .04275. Later corresponding masses .65306/.35694,.28431/.00493,.03247.
Seen-ranking remaining potential .27276/.29611; new-user/global-known remaining .25803/.27938. These are diagnostic oracle gaps, not learnable guarantees.
Original shortlist internal ranking gap .33966/.35871 exceeds missing-candidate oracle gap .23388/.24926.
Weekly retrieval raises top5 candidate oracle .74708→.78135 and .72058→.75331, but achieved top5 MAP decreases .001031/.002063 after refit.
Missing top5 pairs mostly user-new but globally observed:1146of1363 main,1270of1410 later. Only217/140 are globally unobserved.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Use fixed current pairs first: decompose false positives and per-source AP; evaluate a prespecified seen-versus-new-known gate or airing-level probability of one uninterrupted>80percent overlap, with a separate calibration check for new-known pairs. Measure incremental actual AP, not only retrieval coverage. Expand candidates only after signal improves conditional ranking.
hypotheses.budget: Saved-prediction decomposition completed in under2seconds; further conditional diagnostics <=2min/1GB. One targeted fitted gate/airing model only after approval, with fixed setup and<=10min/2GB budget proposal.
hypotheses.strategy_change: Prioritize reliable seen ordering and calibrated new-known relevance; avoid investing primarily in globally cold item machinery or another topK increase. Conditional completion scoring may connect historical channel habits with programme airtime better than total expected minutes.
hypotheses.risk: Source-only oracles overlap for all80 and cannot be summed. For top5 they are additive, but assume perfect knowledge of future labels. Training only current shortlist can undersample new-known positives; any target-informed training-pair sampling must remain confined to fitting labels and clearly documented. No future metadata beyond permitted schedule availability/channel/time.

proposed_decision_gate.primary: Predeclare one hypothesis, fixed candidate and target policy, and a material-gain threshold before fitting; retain v3 otherwise.
proposed_decision_gate.robustness: Report both all80/top5count80 on both windows, plus unchanged all-user and nonempty-user summaries. Do not silently exclude empty users. Until scorer is known, prefer gains whose direction is consistent across plausible targets; tradeoffs must be explicitly surfaced rather than choosing favorable proxy.
proposed_decision_gate.evidence: Paired user-level AP changes and uncertainty, source slice diagnostics, and actual ranking improvement. Candidateoracle alone cannot approve an expensive round or submission.
proposed_decision_gate.limitation: Reused overlapping windows do not become independent tests because a new protocol is written. User bootstrap quantifies sample variability, not hidden-target uncertainty or extrapolation risk.
